next_question: On the same credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, change the acquisition MECHANISM from same-host link-following BFS to SITE-NATIVE DISCOVERY channels (robots.txt sitemap directives, sitemap.xml, on-site search/query URLs, RSS/Atom feeds, and JSON-LD/structured-data enumeration): over a frozen multi-host pool that is separately confirmed to contain DEEP (hop>=3) state items on at least two distinct hosts/engines, what fraction of those DEEP items can be reached in <= K preregistered GETs (e.g. K=3: one discovery GET plus the item-page GET) using a site-native discovery channel alone, versus only by traversing the hop>=3 shortest path? Preregistered falsifier, arithmetically checkable before freeze and satisfiable in BOTH directions: if the O(1)-reachable fraction of DEEP state items is >= a preregistered materiality threshold (e.g. 0.50) on >=2 engines, then shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier for discovery-enabled acquisition and persistent path caching is not the optimization target (effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion); if that fraction is below the threshold, then even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence of paths/procedures retains a measurable, depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from a real re-derivation cost. This is materially orthogonal to EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378 because it measures a different acquisition mechanism rather than re-scoring a link-following level-order estimator whose DEEP/NEAR ratio is forced by construction (VN-V9/VF-03). If the Global Research Director instead prefers the maintenance/invalidation axis, the alternative live question is: how does the cost of keeping a persisted path/procedure VALID between episodes (re-validation GETs/bytes plus the stale-replay false-accept rate) scale with hop and elapsed time relative to re-derivation.
why_next: WHY THIS DIRECTION AND NOT ANOTHER. This packet executed the parent mandate EXP-FRONTIER-37385647440's next_question (convert the parent's hop<=1 non-result into a hop-depth cost-scaling law) and it did so VALIDLY: controls live-PASS, admission gate PASS (26 DEEP / 419 NEAR / 4 hosts site rows), K=2 sessions agree, audit PASS, and the frozen rule returned GROWING (R_req=5.27, R_bytes=7.31 at M=3.0). But the measurement's own producer and auditor both bound it: RED is an item-blind FIFO BFS prefix that the frozen baseline-ordering proof forces to be >= the persisted-path arm, so the GROWING ratio is substantially a property of the level-order estimator's branching factor, not independent evidence about Web acquisition economics (VN-V9/VF-03); the direct persisted-path arm is near-linear in hop (requests ratio 2.0, h+1 by construction); and every admitted DEEP item is single-host/single-engine mdBook (VN-V8/VF-02) with the non-mdBook roots admitting zero DEEP items within B=250/D=6 (VN-V13). So the acquisition-cost-scaling question is now bounded at its estimator ceiling, and re-scoring the same level-order estimator would be a same-basin repeat that the parent handoff explicitly warned against. The materially orthogonal and decision-changing move is to change the acquisition MECHANISM, not the estimator: ask whether site-native discovery channels (sitemaps, on-site search, feeds, structured data) let a fresh agent reach a DEEP state item in O(1) GETs without any prior crawl. This is orthogonal because it measures a different acquisition route entirely (site-provided discovery, not link-following enumeration), it directly attacks the assumption that depth costs h+1, it needs no browser/Docker/model key/credential/write verb (GET-only stdlib), and it is decision-changing in both directions: if discovery makes DEEP items O(1)-reachable, persistence of paths is not the optimization target and effort belongs in discovery/substrate expansion; if not, persistence retains a real depth-dependent amortization surface. The alternative I considered and left as an explicit option for the Director is the maintenance/invalidation axis (re-validation cost plus stale-replay false-accept rate as a function of hop and elapsed time), which is also orthogonal but overlaps the C-FRESHNESS thread owned by graph and is closer to an instrument repair of this thread. I did NOT propose another tokenizer/latency/dollar upgrade, another five-class or stationarity taxonomy, another threshold or materiality-factor retune, or a re-run of the frozen DEEP/NEAR ratio, because all of those are repairs or same-basin repeats, none is authorized by this lane, and none would discriminate the O(1)-versus-depth-growing question.
